title: Baseline check: fractions & decimals on a number line (10 questions)

questions.q: A number line from 0 to 1 is cut into 4 equal parts. What fraction is point A? [img:base-q1]
questions.why: 4 equal parts = fourths. Point A is on the 1st mark, so it is 1/4.

questions.q: A number line from 0 to 1 is cut into 5 equal parts. What fraction is point B? [img:base-q2]
questions.why: 5 equal parts = fifths. B is on the 3rd mark: 3/5.

questions.q: A number line from 0 to 1 is cut into 8 equal parts. What fraction is point C? [img:base-q3]
questions.why: 8 equal parts = eighths. C is on the 5th mark: 5/8.

questions.q: A number line from 0 to 1 is cut into 10 equal parts. Write point D as a decimal. [img:base-q4]
questions.why: 10 equal parts = tenths. D is on the 7th mark: 7/10 = 0.7.

questions.q: This number line goes from 0 to 2. Which point is 1.5? [img:base-q5]
questions.why: Each part is 0.5: A = 0.5, B = 1, C = 1.5.

questions.q: This number line goes from 1 to 4. Which point is the best estimate for 2.9? [img:base-q6]
questions.why: 2.9 is just under 3, which is 2 whole jumps from 1. Point B sits just before the 2nd mark (3).

questions.q: The jumps are tenths (0.1). The numbers 2.6 and 3.0 are marked. What number goes in the ? box at the end? [img:base-q7]
The jumps are tenths (0.1). The ends are 4.3 and 5.3. Point M is 6 jumps from 4.3. What number is M? [img:base-q8]
A number line from 3 to 4 is cut into 5 equal parts. What is the size of each jump? [img:base-q9]
questions.why: 1 whole cut into 5 equal parts: each is 1/5 = 0.2.

questions.q: Point P is exactly halfway between 0.4 and 0.5. What is its value? [img:base-q10]
